claims.claim: CRI reported FY2026 totals of 188 invention disclosures, 333 patent applications, 66 granted patents, 12 executed licenses/options, and nine new companies.
claims.correction: Say “CRI reported” and use “executed 12 licenses and options.”

claims.claim: CRI reported that spinouts raised an additional $25.7 million in FY2026.
claims.correction: Retain attribution; do not characterize the money as equity financing.

claims.claim: Since CRI’s 2011 creation, Northeastern reported 1,874 disclosures, 799 granted patents, and 122 companies built on Northeastern research.
claims.correction: Use “reported” and retain “built on Northeastern research.”

claims.claim: Of 122 companies, 61 were active, nine acquired, and 39 had established operations in Massachusetts.
claims.correction: Replace “established operations” with CRI’s narrower wording: “39 had set up in Massachusetts.”

claims.claim: Ninety-four Northeastern students completed co-ops at spinout companies.
claims.correction: Attribute the count to CRI; no period is specified in the sentence.

claims.claim: InLoop is a Northeastern spinout founded by Jeffrey Lipton, Jacob Miske, and Brett Emery.
InLoop is developing an in-clinic, customized-orthotics workflow using 3D printing and looping coil metal foam, with a claimed 24-hour turnaround.
claims.correction: Say “CRI says InLoop is developing” and “claims a 24-hour turnaround”; do not imply clinical availability or outcomes.

claims.claim: InLoop was one of the top three teams from 12 at The Engine’s Spring 2026 Blueprint Showcase.
claims.correction: Frame this as a cohort/showcase result, not technology validation.

claims.claim: Tantu Therapeutics is developing microbe-based therapies for IBD.
claims.correction: Use “developing”; do not call it an approved or clinically proven treatment.

claims.claim: Fourier Thermal Solutions is developing thermal-management technology and participated in NSIN Emerge, received a $75,000 MassCEC Catalyst award, and joined a MassChallenge cohort.
claims.correction: Use “CRI reported” and avoid presenting affiliations as commercial traction.

claims.claim: Ada IQ completed Techstars Boston, received SBIR Phase I funding with CRI grant-writing support, and partnered with PTC.
claims.correction: Say “partnered with product-design firm PTC”; do not claim partnership revenue or deployment.

claims.claim: Pathfind develops deep-learning model-compression methods intended to run AI on simpler devices.
claims.correction: Use “intended/enables,” not benchmarked performance or deployed use.

claims.claim: CellOS targets automated 5G/6G control; Rheopoint applies AI to fluid mechanics/materials discovery; ViralNPQ develops viral-measurement tools.
claims.correction: Describe them as CRI/lab development projects, not completed products.

claims.claim: An unnamed Northeastern spinout is preparing technology for a 2028 lunar mission.
claims.correction: Name the company, payload, mission provider, and primary mission source—or omit the claim.

claims.claim: Tadavo was built from NSF-funded Northeastern research and is led in the cited post by CEO Tim Penasack and faculty founder Tucker Marion.
claims.correction: Attribute to CRI’s promotional post; “led by” is safer than implying independently verified corporate roles.

claims.claim: CRI reported Tadavo had 150-plus brand discussions, 40-plus active prospects, five pending patents, and a live MVP focused on footwear, apparel, and sporting goods.
claims.correction: Label every metric as Tadavo/CRI-reported, unaudited company traction.

claims.claim: Zepsor is commercializing zero-power infrared sensors that remain in standby until activated by a target signal.
claims.correction: Keep it as a 2025 CRI update; do not fold its CES 2025 and April 2025 funding milestones into FY2026 without a fiscal-year mapping.

counterevidence.finding: No retrieved independent technical, clinical, customer-use, or comparative-performance evidence validates InLoop’s turnaround, workflow, or patient benefit. The available evidence is a CRI promotional post.

The strongest directly relevant Northeastern reporting describes related engineered-probiotic work as laboratory proof of concept, with live-animal work next; a 2021 Tantu announcement called the company pre-seed and discussed an aim to reach clinical proof of concept, not achieved human efficacy.
Accelerator participation, grants, discussions, prospects, pending patents, and an MVP substantiate activity—not revenue, adoption, independently audited financing, or product performance.
CRI says 39 companies “have set up in Massachusetts”; that does not establish the stronger claim that each has ongoing Massachusetts operations.

open_questions.question: What exact dates define Northeastern FY2026, and what instruments comprise the reported $25.7 million?
Which nine ventures constitute FY2026 launches, and what company-level method supports active/acquired/Massachusetts classifications?
What prototype, podiatry-site, patient-testing, manufacturing-capacity, and product-clearance evidence exists for InLoop?
What is Tantu’s current candidate, preclinical/clinical stage, and current operating status?
Which spinout, mission, payload, launch provider, and 2028 target are being referenced?
Can Tadavo document its stated discussions, prospects, patent applications, and live-MVP usage?
